Since a quadratic is determined by its values at \(-2,0,2\), Lagrange interpolation gives
\[
f(x)=p\frac{x(x-2)}{8}+q\frac{4-x^2}{4}+r\frac{x(x+2)}{8}.
\]

For \(x\in[-2,2]\),
\[
|f(x)|
\le 2\left(\frac{|x(x-2)|}{8}+\frac{4-x^2}{4}+\frac{|x(x+2)|}{8}\right).
\]

On \([-2,2]\), one checks that
\[
|x(x-2)|+|x(x+2)|=4|x|.
\]
Therefore
\[
|f(x)|
\le 2\left(\frac{4|x|}{8}+\frac{4-x^2}{4}\right)
=2+|x|-\frac{x^2}{2}.
\]

Let \(s=|x|\in[0,2]\). Then
\[
2+|x|-\frac{x^2}{2}=2+s-\frac{s^2}{2}
=\frac52-\frac12(s-1)^2\le \frac52.
\]

So for every admissible quadratic,
\[
|f(x)|\le \frac52.
\]

This bound is attained, for example, by
\[
f(x)=-\frac12x^2+x+2.
\]
Indeed,
\[
f(0)=2,\qquad f(2)=2,\qquad f(-2)=-2,
\]
and
\[
f(1)=\frac52.
\]

Hence the maximum possible value is

\[
\boxed{\frac52}
\]
